text:
maya: heads-up — last night we had an incident where hosted nodepools in us-west-2 filled up and the cluster-autoscaler brought up GPU nodes in the wrong pool, causing ~8m cold-starts for Dedicated tenants. noticed requests were routed to hosted because of affinity scoring differences.

raj: ugh. any logs/trace?

maya: yes — autoscaler event log shows it evaluated capacity by label `gpu-type: v100` but ignored `redwood.dedicated=true` annotation on the namespace. autoscaler config uses `expander: least-waste` which prioritized capacity packing. snippet: 
```
Event:   Normal  ScaleUp  50s (x3 over 7m)  cluster-autoscaler  Pod default/gpu-serving triggered scale-up: no nodes are available that match pod's nodeSelector
Node labels considered: gpu-type=v100, zone=us-west-2b
Namespace annotations: redwood.dedicated=true
```

linh: that's because our node-template filters only add label selectors, not namespace-aware taints. autoscaler doesn't know about "tenant ownership" unless we encode it into `nodeGroup` heuristics.

sam: what if we add a `preferredPools` annotation on the pod/namespace so autoscaler tries dedicated first then hosted fallback? like an ordered list.

elena: the challenge is correctness vs fragility. if dedicated is empty but takes 3m to provision and hosted can pop in 20s, we may want to prefer hosted for low-latency SLAs. we need a policy that balances latency SLO vs isolation.

maya: agreed. proposal from my side: introduce two mechanisms — 1) namespace-level `redwood.pool-preference: dedicated,hosted` annotation, and 2) autoscaler plugin that respects preference but applies a timeout window (prewarm-window). if dedicated can't satisfy within Xs, fall back to hosted automatically.

raj: sounds reasonable. what's the fallback timeout?

maya: thinking 45s default for interactive traffic (chat/generation) and 300s for batch. can be per-route. also track a metric `warm-minutes` to charge for prewarmed capacity to tenants.

linh: implementation notes: autoscaler currently supports `scaleUpDelay` and `scaleDownDelay`. we'll add `preferenceTimeouts` keyed by annotation. minimal changes: in pod scheduling evaluation, if pool-preference present, mark preferred nodegroups with soft-priority and start a timer when scale-up triggered. if timer expires, allow non-preferred nodegroups.

sam: can we do this without changing upstream autoscaler? maybe a small controller that intercepts unschedulable pods and creates a `PoolClaim` CRD that maps to nodegroups, then manages the timeout and failover. keeps upstream pristine.

maya: i like the CRD approach. easier to iterate. quick sketch: 
```
apiVersion: inference.redwood.ai/v1
kind: PoolClaim
metadata:
  name: claim-<pod>-<ts>
spec:
  namespace: customer-a
  preferredPools: ["dedicated-usw2-v100", "hosted-usw2-v100"]
  timeoutSeconds: 45
```

elena: +1 to CRD. also add two safety checks: (a) network egress tag propagation so hosted nodes still get the right VPC egress for tenant data, and (b) enforce KMS access only on dedicated nodes for private deployments.

ops-bot: Deploy event: autoscaler-config v0.34 promoted to canary in us-west-2 at 2026-03-17T02:12:00Z :rocket:

raj: what about cost visibility? if we prewarm dedicated nodes for 45s and they stay unused, chargebacks should be transparent. we need per-namespace `prewarm_cpu_seconds` and `prewarm_gpu_seconds` metrics exported.

maya: agreed — propose adding tags to Prometheus metrics: `pool_claim_id` and `pool_type`. billing can ingest those metrics. also dashboard will show "wasted prewarm minutes" per tenant.

linh: small network caveat — when failing over from dedicated->hosted, we hit a cross-AZ ENI attach delay if hosted nodes are in different AZ. ensure preferredPools list is AZ-aware or we prewarm in same AZ when possible.

sam: action items then: (1) maya + linh prototype PoolClaim CRD + controller (2w), (2) raj wire up metrics & billing tags (1w), (3) elena run security checklist for KMS/egress on hosted fallback (3d), (4) ops-bot run canary tests for 30m after deploy.

elena: I'm ok with that timeline. also please add a canary test that writes/reads a small secret via KMS to confirm fallback path is restricted.

maya: noted. I'll open a PR with the CRD sketch and a simple controller that watches unschedulable pods and honors `redwood.pool-preference`. tagging it with `RFC: pool-claim-controller`

raj: sgtm. thanks. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Incident digest: there were 12 affected requests between 2026-03-16T23:50:00Z and 2026-03-17T00:10:00Z. median extra latency 340s. Follow-up: see thread above for proposed mitigation.

maya: thanks team — will post RFC link here when PR is up.
